did_you_know.text: Did you know? The chapter opens with the word of the LORD coming to Jonah son of Amittai, presenting Jonah as a prophet receiving a divine mission.
Did you know? Nineveh is described in the chapter as “the great city,” and the reason for sending Jonah there is that the wickedness of its inhabitants has come before the LORD.
Did you know? Instead of going to Nineveh, Jonah goes down to Joppa, finds a ship bound for Tarshish, pays the fare, and boards it to flee from the presence of the LORD.
Did you know? The storm is not described as merely a random event: the LORD hurls a great wind upon the sea, and the ship is about to break apart.
Did you know? While the sailors pray and throw the ship’s cargo into the sea to lighten it, Jonah goes down into the hold and falls asleep.
Did you know? It is the captain who wakes Jonah and tells him to get up and pray, hoping that the god he prays to will save them so that they will not perish.
Did you know? The sailors cast lots to determine on whose account this trouble has come, and the lot falls on Jonah.
Did you know? Jonah identifies himself as a Hebrew and declares that he worships the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land.
Did you know? After Jonah tells them that he is fleeing from the presence of the LORD, the sailors become extremely frightened and ask him, “What have you done?”
Did you know? After Jonah is thrown into the sea and the storm subsides, the sailors fear the LORD greatly, offer sacrifices to him, and make vows.
